# civo_volume (Resource)

Provides a Civo volume which can be attached to an instance in order to provide expanded storage.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get network
data "civo_network" "default_network" {
    label = "Default"
}

# Create volume
resource "civo_volume" "db" {
    name = "backup-data"
    size_gb = 5
    network_id = data.civo_network.default_network.id
    depends_on = [
      data.civo_network.default_network
    ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A name that you wish to use to refer to this volume
- `network_id` (String) The network that the volume belongs to
- `size_gb` (Number) A minimum of 1 and a maximum of your available disk space from your quota specifies the size of the volume in gigabytes. Increases are applied in place: on a detached volume, and on a volume attached to a running instance when its volume type supports online expansion. Otherwise the API refuses the resize with `volume_onlie_resize` (detach the volume or move it to an expandable volume type) or `volume_resize_requires_running_instance` (start the instance). Decreases are rejected at plan time; recreate the volume with `terraform apply -replace` for a smaller size.

### Optional

- `region` (String) The region for the volume, if not declare we use the region in declared in the provider.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `volume_type` (String) The type of the volume

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `mount_point` (String) The mount point of the volume (from instance's perspective)

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `update` (String) How long to wait for a resize to be confirmed. Defaults to `60m`.

## Resizing

> **Behaviour change.** Earlier provider versions detached an attached volume to resize it and re-attached it at boot. This version resizes in place and never detaches a volume on your behalf: an attached volume on a volume type without online expansion is refused by the API with `volume_onlie_resize`, and the error says what to do. See [Upgrade notes](#upgrade-notes).

Increasing `size_gb` resizes the volume in place. A detached volume is resized offline; a volume attached to a running instance is grown online when its volume type supports expansion. The provider then follows the resize until the API confirms the new size and fails the apply when the platform reports that the resize failed (for example `InsufficientStorage` or `Timeout`). On an API that does not yet report the delivered size, the apply warns that the resize was accepted but could not be confirmed.

If an earlier resize is still running when the apply starts (for example after a previous apply timed out while following it), the provider waits for it to settle before issuing the new one, within the same `update` timeout.

The API refuses a resize it cannot perform:

- `volume_onlie_resize` (the code's spelling matches the API): the volume is attached and its volume type does not support online expansion. Detach the volume, or move it to a volume type that supports expansion.
- `volume_resize_requires_running_instance`: the volume is attached to a stopped instance. Start the instance.

Decreasing `size_gb` is rejected at plan time. To get a smaller volume, recreate it with `terraform apply -replace=civo_volume.<name>`.

The wait is bounded by the resource's `update` timeout, 60 minutes by default. The platform bounds each phase of a resize at 15 minutes and reports a `Timeout` failure when one stalls, so the apply normally ends well before that; lower it with a `timeouts` block when you want to give up sooner:

```hcl
resource "civo_volume" "data" {
  # ...
  timeouts {
    update = "20m"
  }
}
```

### Upgrade notes

Before this behaviour, a `size_gb` change on an attached volume detached the volume, resized it and re-attached it at boot, taking the instance's storage offline and turning a hot-plugged attachment into a boot attachment. The provider no longer does that. An attached volume on a volume type without online expansion now fails with `volume_onlie_resize` instead of being detached behind your back.

To resize such a volume, detach it explicitly, then resize, then re-attach:

- If the attachment is managed by a `civo_volume_attachment`, remove that resource from the configuration and apply, change `size_gb` and apply, then add the attachment back and apply.
- Alternatively, move the volume to a volume type that supports online expansion and resize it attached.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# using ID
terraform import civo_volume.db 506f78a4-e098-11e5-ad9f-000f53306ae1
```
